To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the first moments of the scalar, axial-vector and pseudo-scalar correlators in third order of αs are known and that they are available in numerical form for arbitrary values of the heavy-quark mass.
we calculated the third order perturbative corrections to moments of the heavy quark current correlation functions.

the first moments of the scalar and pseudo-scalar current correlators are known to four-loop order in the strong coupling constant and the first moment of axial-vector correlator is known to three-loop order.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of moments of the current-current correlators of heavy quarks in QCD.
the calculation of the first moment of heavy quark vector, axial-vector and pseudo-scalar current correlators in perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD).
the calculation of the moments of the heavy quark current correlation function at four-loop order.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theoretical uncertainty of the QCD scale ΛQCD is reduced by 20% to 30%.
the current situation is not yet satisfactory and that further progress can be made.

the current status of the theory of moments of heavy quark currents at the four-loop level is such that the theoretical uncertainty of the lattice calculations of these quantities can be reduced significantly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have computed the first three moments of the scalar and pseudo-scalar correlators and the first moment of axial-vector correlator at four-loop order, which are the highest order available in the literature.
the perturbative expansion for these quantities is convergent and that it is well possible to obtain results for the first moment with an accuracy of 1% in αs.
we are now in a position to provide a reliable estimate of the QCD corrections for the first moment at the level of the next-to-next-to-leading order.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the theoretical uncertainties due to missing higher-order terms are significantly reduced for the moments of heavy quark currents.

the uncertainty due to higher orders in αs is reduced by a factor of about 3 for the scalar current, by a factor of 2 for the axial-vector and by a factor of more than 3 for the pseudo-scalar current.
the uncertainty of the theoretical predictions can be reduced by a factor of 2-3 by taking into account the four-loop corrections.
